segments.name: Cause-driven sharers
segments.description: Progressive, socially conscious Facebook users (mostly women, 25–44, college-educated) who follow Upworthy and share its posts to signal values and rally friends around causes.

values.value: working professional / nonprofit or education worker
Facebook feed from friends and liked pages
progressive outlets and email lists (MoveOn, Upworthy email)
moderate attention: will watch a 3–5 minute video if the cause matters
checks Facebook several times a day
low: forgives curiosity-gap headlines when the cause is good
frequent sharer (shares several posts a week)

needs: A story about a social-justice cause (equality, LGBT rights, poverty, health care) that makes them feel something
Something worth sharing that says who they are to friends
A clear takeaway or action (donate, sign, spread the word)
A credible, non-cynical framing of an issue
barriers: Headline feels manipulative or oversold relative to the content
Cause or framing that seems shallow, corporate or off-mission
Topics they have already seen shared many times
Content that is cruel, mocking or divisive in tone

source.evidence: Women are also particularly likely to use Facebook compared with men, a trend that continues from prior years.
source.note: Pew 2014 Facebook-wide finding (direction only); the stronger female tilt for this cause-sharing segment is my estimate. No Upworthy-specific gender split found in opened pages.

segments.name: Feel-good incidental scrollers
segments.description: Mainstream Facebook users, many of them parents and older adults, who meet Upworthy posts incidentally in their feed via friends' shares and click on heartwarming, inspiring or surprising stories rather than politics.

values.value: low attention to spare: quick taps between other activities
moderate: will watch a short video
checks Facebook several times a day

needs: An uplifting, emotional story (kindness, kids, families, underdogs)
Something entertaining or that improves their day
A story a friend already shared or liked
Clear, simple language with an obvious emotional payoff
barriers: Headline that is vague about what the post is
Long or heavy content when they are just checking in on friends
Content that feels like an ad or a fundraising pitch

source.evidence: Women are also particularly likely to use Facebook compared with men, a trend that continues from prior years.
source.note: Pew 2014 Facebook-wide finding (direction only), reused for this segment; magnitude is my estimate.

source.evidence: about a third, 34%, of Facebook news consumers are 18-29 years old, compared with only 20% of other Facebook users.
source.note: Pew 2013 whole-audience figures for Facebook news consumers; this segment sits between news consumers and other users, so shifted older.

source.evidence: About two-thirds (65%) of those who get news on Facebook say they visit the site several times a day
source.note: Pew 2013 whole-audience figure, nudged down for this lighter-use segment.

segments.name: Young media-savvy skeptics
segments.description: Urban 18–29 college students and young professionals who see Upworthy posts constantly, click out of curiosity but mock the curiosity-gap headline formula and rarely share unless the content beats the hype.

values.value: constant scrolling, several times a day

needs: Concrete, specific headlines that say what the content is
Genuinely surprising or funny content, not just emotional
Content that won't embarrass them if shared
Substance or original reporting behind the packaging
barriers: Curiosity-gap formulas ("you won't believe", "will blow your mind")
Repackaged videos they have already seen elsewhere

source.evidence: Women are also particularly likely to use Facebook compared with men, a trend that continues from prior years.
source.note: Pew 2014 Facebook-wide direction; for this skeptic segment I estimate an even split (critics in press coverage skew male), so weight is largely my estimate.

source.note: Pew 2013 whole-audience figure; this segment is defined as the young end of that audience, so 18-29 is heavily weighted.
